candidates.claim: For the two TP1/DP4/EP4 engines, first inspect the effective image, router policy, API2 request path, and internal DP rank selection to establish whether rank-aware prefix routing is already active. If absent, test a bounded policy that prefers a rank holding an exact reusable prefix only while its estimated queue load stays within a chosen skew limit; otherwise it falls back to load-only routing. API2 must preserve or convey the rank choice through the internal DP4 decision, since replica affinity alone cannot guarantee a local cache hit. The 75% cacheability figure is a target, not an observed hit rate. Shadow routing should first determine whether avoidable rank-local misses exist. Predict better goodput only where saved prefill work outweighs skew and routing cost.

candidates.claim: First inspect the effective scheduler commit and runtime settings to establish whether adaptive prefill admission already exists. If absent, test a scheduler-local prefill budget that decreases when active decodes approach their measured iteration deadlines and increases when decode pressure eases. Keep the global token budget fixed; bound each prefill request’s waiting time so decode protection cannot starve TTFT. This transfers the pressure-dependent budget mechanism described by P-PAS, while adding an explicit deadline and waiting bound for the R7b objective. The source reports results on other model and GPU configurations, so neither a B200 crossover nor an effect size is known. A cheap trace analysis should first test whether prefill-bearing iterations coincide with decode deadline misses before any GPU replay.
